about: Source of truth for Akashic delivery work. WORKPLAN.md is generated from this file. See CLAUDE.md for the protocol.

track_notes.LEGACY: Retire Supabase, Cloudflare and R2. Repo-side removal can happen now; the infrastructure deletions are gated on the archive being duplicated and on the Pages cutover. LEG-01 is independent of every gate and should happen today.
track_notes.DOCS: Make the documentation true. Cheap, high-value, and it is what stops the next agent inheriting a false picture.
track_notes.SHIP: Hard requirements for a paid v1.0. Most of the remaining calendar time lives here, in items only the owner can do.
track_notes.DIFF: Capability beyond what competitors offer. Order set by decision: share link, then Vision curation, then the book.
track_notes.QUALITY: Tests, types, CI, localisation, accessibility. Localisation and accessibility are in v1.0 by decision.

decisions.what: The web client is frozen as a showcase view
decisions.why: Keep signed-out showcase and comments; hide every native-only write behind one guard and delete the rest. About 2-3 days instead of 12, and it closes the bug where six components pretend to save. Decided 2026-07-26.

decisions.what: Differentiation order: share link, then Vision curation, then the book
decisions.why: The share link is broken rather than absent, it carries a live privacy leak, and it is the gate that makes the beta measurement possible at all. The book's value is conditional on curation: 939 photos with 449 unique images produces a book nobody wants. Decided 2026-07-26.

decisions.what: Norwegian localisation and accessibility both ship in v1.0
decisions.why: Selling Norwegian-first with an English-only binary is the likelier one-star, and accessibility is harder to retro-fit across 50 view files later. About 8-9 days added before submission. Decided 2026-07-26.

decisions.what: No live tracking, no print pipeline, no Android, no custom backend
decisions.why: Carried forward from COMMERCIALIZATION-PLAN section 9. Live tracking is Polarsteps' moat and belongs to during the trip; this product is about after.

gates.name: Paid Applications agreement, banking and tax
gates.detail: 1-2 weeks, entirely outside the build queue, and no in-app purchase can go live without it. The one item that can silently add two weeks. SHIP-12.

gates.name: External beta
gates.detail: About three weeks minimum: at least 7 of 10 households creating a journey unaided and 5 finishing and handing one over. The largest calendar item and nothing shortens it. SHIP-17.

gates.name: One month before deleting DATA infrastructure (hosting rollback waived)
gates.detail:
TWO CLOCKS, and the owner waived one on 2026-07-27.
  * HOSTING clock — WAIVED. It existed only to keep a DNS revert to Cloudflare useful. The owner does not want a rollback path, so the Cloudflare Pages project, deploy.yml and the Cloudflare tokens go as soon as the cutover is verified. Worst case is akashic.no down for a while and a re-deploy to Pages; no data is at stake.
  * DATA clock — STANDS, earliest 2026-08-24. This one is not about rollback convenience: R2 holds the 16 GiB / 8147-object archive and Supabase the source rows, and its real gate is LEG-02 (a verified second physical medium), not the calendar. Deleting either before LEG-02 passes is irreversible loss of the family's photographs. Once LEG-02 and LEG-03/LEG-04 are done, whether to also waive the calendar month is the owner's call.
  Does not apply to LEG-01: nothing reads the Worker.

gates.name: App Review
gates.detail: 1-3 days plus a 3-5 day buffer for one rejection round.

tasks.title: Execute the GitHub Pages + DNS cutover (T4.2, T4.3)
tasks.done_when: https://akashic.no serves the production build from GitHub Pages with a valid certificate for the domain, and privacy/terms/support/AASA resolve over HTTPS.
tasks.why:
Nothing Cloudflare-hosted can be deleted until this lands — deploy.yml still deploys the live site on every push to main. The runbook is complete and two of its stated blockers are already closed: the AASA Team ID is filled in, and netlify.toml was removed by d331970.

DNS DESTINATION DECIDED 2026-07-27: Domeneshop's own DNS, not GoDaddy. whois confirms the registrar is Domeneshop AS (REG42-NORID, Oslo), so the NS delegation is changed there regardless -- keeping DNS in the same place avoids splitting one domain across two consoles, and avoids GoDaddy's account-wide API keys, which cannot be scoped to a single domain. Measured TTLs, which size the cutover: A records are already at 300 s, and the .no registry's NS delegation TTL is 7200 s. During an NS change the OLD nameservers keep answering until that expires, so there is no dark window -- only up to ~2 h where some resolvers reach Cloudflare (old build) and some reach Pages (new build). Both render an empty globe until SHIP-10B publishes something, so the split is invisible to visitors. That makes now the cheapest moment this cutover will ever have.

DOMENESHOP API LIMITS, measured 2026-07-27 with a live token. The API's own feature list is: list domains, list invoices, CRUD DNS records, CRUD HTTP forwards. That is all. Specifically NOT automatable:
  * enabling the DNS service -- GET /v0/domains/2216481/dns returns 404 resource:unknown while services.dns is false, so there is no zone to write into until it is switched on in the web UI;
  * changing the delegation -- `nameservers` appears only in the READ schema of the Domain object.
So the owner's irreducible step is one switch: activate Domeneshop DNS for akashic.no, which normally sets the delegation to ns1/ns2/ns3.hyp.net at the same time. The nine records are then agent work via POST /v0/domains/2216481/dns.
Domain id is 2216481. A token scoped to this account reaches EXACTLY ONE domain (akashic.no), which is why the account-wide-key objection raised against GoDaddy does not bite here -- verified by GET /v0/domains before anything was written.
SEQUENCING: activating DNS points the delegation at an EMPTY zone, so add the records immediately after. The 7200 s NS TTL means old resolvers keep reaching Cloudflare meanwhile, so the exposure is small and the owner has accepted downtime.

ZONE BUILT AND VERIFIED 2026-07-27, propagation pending. Owner ticked 'Bruk Domeneshops navnetjenere'; services.dns flipped to true and Domeneshop pre-imported Cloudflare's 2 A + 2 AAAA. Those four were UPDATED to GitHub's addresses rather than deleted (honouring the no-deletions commitment), and five more created: 4 A (185.199.108-111.153), 4 AAAA (2606:50c0:8000-8003::153), www CNAME -> chaerem.github.io., all ttl 300. Verified authoritatively against ns1.hyp.net -- exactly the four GitHub A records and nothing else -- so no propagation wait was needed to confirm correctness. Pages serves 200 with environment:"production" when resolved via the new addresses; /privacy, /terms, /support all 200; www 301s to the apex. DS records at the registry: 0, so ticking DNSSEC did not create a validation hazard. ALL THAT REMAINS is delegation propagation: Domeneshop warns up to 4 h to begin and a further 24 h to be visible everywhere, which is longer than the 7200 s NS TTL alone suggested -- Norid registry updates are not instant. Close this once dig +short akashic.no NS returns the hyp.net servers.

OPERATIONAL NOTE discovered 2026-07-27: the `github-pages` environment has a deployment branch policy allowing ONLY `main` (custom_branch_policies: true, branch_policies: ['main']). So a workflow_dispatch of deploy-pages.yml against any other ref builds fine and then fails at the deploy job with 'Branch ... is not allowed to deploy to github-pages due to environment protection rules'. That is a safety net, not a fault: a feature branch can never become the live Pages build, which is worth knowing before someone 'fixes' the failing job. It also means the only way to deploy is to merge to main.

REOPENED 2026-07-27 -- I closed this prematurely and the site is currently BROKEN over HTTPS.
Measured state, pinned to GitHub's addresses so there is no ambiguity: http 200 serving the correct production bundle on both IPv4 and IPv6, and **https 000 on both** -- GitHub Pages presents CN=*.github.io (Let's Encrypt) because it has issued NO certificate for akashic.no. The pages API shows no https_certificate key at all.
DNS is not the problem and is fully correct: 8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1 and 9.9.9.9 all return the four GitHub A records and the four AAAA. So a visitor on any normal resolver reaches GitHub and gets a TLS failure, while http:// works.
TWO MISTAKES OF MINE worth recording. First, I verified the cutover over HTTP and called it complete; HTTPS is the state that matters and I had not checked it. Second, when I later saw 'https 200' I reported success without checking the content -- it was CLOUDFLARE answering my machine from a stale cache (Tailscale resolver at 100.100.100.100), serving the OLD bundle with the OLD development token and a Google Trust Services cert. Reading the bundle's environment string is what caught it. A status code is not a verification.
I also removed and re-added the custom domain to nudge provisioning, which is the documented remedy but may have restarted GitHub's clock. The certificate was already absent before that, so it was not working either way -- but I cannot rule out having reset a check that was nearly done. Do NOT nudge again; repeated re-adds restart it.
Close this when `openssl s_client -connect akashic.no:443 -servername akashic.no` shows subject=CN=akashic.no issued by Let's Encrypt (GitHub's issuer), NOT Google Trust Services (Cloudflare's).
refs: docs/github-pages-cutover.md — complete zero-downtime runbook with rollback
deploy-pages.yml is correct and complete; only its trigger needs flipping
notes: 2026-07-27 THE STATE IS ANOMALOUS, NOT WAITING — and this corrects what I told the owner earlier the same day. The Pages UI shows "DNS check in progress", which reads as an ordinary waiting state. It is not. `gh api repos/CHaerem/Akashic/pages/health` returns is_valid: true, is_https_eligible: true, caa_error: null and reason: null for BOTH akashic.no and www.akashic.no — verified across four consecutive calls. So GitHub's own DNS checker PASSES. Per GitHub's documented pipeline (DNS check -> queue job -> Let's Encrypt -> upload -> check mark) a passing check should have produced a certificate record; instead https_certificate is ABSENT from the Pages object — not "new", not "authorization_pending", absent, i.e. none of the twelve documented states. The banner is a stale display, not a live verdict.

2026-07-27 NOTE ON THE HEALTH ENDPOINT: it is evaluated on demand and the FIRST call after a while returns an empty object with no domain/alt_domain keys. That reads exactly like "GitHub cannot see your DNS". Call it two or three times before believing anything. This is why the first research pass on this problem never found the endpoint's verdict and concluded, wrongly, that the DNS check simply had not returned yet.

2026-07-27 RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT, so nobody re-litigates them: extra/conflicting apex records (ANY at the authoritative NS returns only SOA; no CNAME, ALIAS or ANAME; the four A and four AAAA match GitHub's documented set exactly, consistent across 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8/9.9.9.9/OpenDNS/ns1.hyp.net); a Domeneshop wildcard (a random subdomain returns NXDOMAIN); CAA (none at akashic.no and none at the `no` TLD, which is the permissive state); DNSSEC (two DS records, alg 15, and the `ad` flag is set — it validates end to end, so DISABLING IT WOULD BE A SECURITY REGRESSION CHASING A RULED-OUT CAUSE, and it is the loudest suggestion you will find given the same-day migration); Let's Encrypt rate limiting (CT logs show 11 issuances for this domain, all Domeneshop's own, none for the identifier set GitHub would request — so no duplicate-certificate limit can have been hit); a wedged deploy (github-pages deployment 5620695346 succeeded 10:13:13Z); a platform incident (Pages operational); and a permissions artefact hiding the field (the token has admin: true on the repo, so this caller would see it).

2026-07-27 WHAT TO DO, in order. (1) Open Settings -> Pages in a BROWSER, let it load fully, change nothing. Not a placebo: GitHub staff have said this can resolve itself "when you visit the repository settings page", and it is a different code path from the API — the health endpoint has now been called nine times with no certificate record appearing. (2) Poll from the terminal: `gh api repos/CHaerem/Akashic/pages --jq '.https_certificate.state // "ABSENT"'`. ANY value, even "new", is real progress, because it means an order finally exists. (3) DO NOT remove and re-add the domain again today. GitHub's docs say that "will cancel and restart the provisioning process", so each repeat throws away whatever exists and restarts the 24-hour ceiling — and an ABSENT record rather than "new" is consistent with exactly that teardown-without-re-enqueue, so repeating the move risks reproducing the state we are trying to escape. One per 24 hours is the whole budget. (4) NEVER force https_enforced: true. That is the single action that turns a cosmetic problem into a real outage, 301-ing every visitor to a certificate that fails validation.

2026-07-27 IF STILL ABSENT ~24 h AFTER THE RE-ADD, it is genuinely abnormal and the escalation evidence is unusually strong: pages/health green on both legs while https_certificate is absent entirely. The only case with a confirmed resolution was a staff member manually re-triggering provisioning, so that is the remedy with a track record. On a free personal account there may be no Pages support category, in which case a Community Discussion under Pages with the same API output is the route.

Flipping the environment alone leaves a development token pointed at production and turns an empty showcase into an erroring one. The token is correctly a variable rather than a secret: CloudKit JS tokens are public by design (they are inlined into the client bundle) and restricted by origin allowlist, not by secrecy.

TOKEN SCOPING PROVEN 2026-07-27, not assumed. The old SHIP-10 said this 'needs a Console step to mint a production CloudKit JS token' without evidence, so it was worth testing before sending the owner to the Console. Queried CloudKit Web Services directly from the akashic.no origin with the CURRENT token, same container, changing only the environment in the URL path:
  development -> HTTP 200, 0 records
  production  -> HTTP 401 AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, 'please check you have the correct API Token for this container'
So a CloudKit JS API token IS environment-scoped and the existing one cannot be reused. Tested via REST rather than CloudKit JS on purpose: calling CloudKit.configure() twice on one container could have produced the same error for an unrelated reason, and did.

Note for whoever explains this to the owner: the token is NOT a secret. It is compiled into the client bundle and readable by any visitor (grep the live JS). Its protection is the allowed-origins list, which is why akashic.no must be on it. Storing it in `vars` rather than `secrets` is therefore correct, and 'moving it to secrets for safety' would change nothing except how safe it looks.

CORRECTION 2026-07-27, after the owner sent a Console screenshot: the note above concluded the owner-supplied token was 'not valid for this container in either environment'. WRONG. It is a valid Production token for iCloud.no.akashic (name Akashic-ci). Two mistakes produced that conclusion:

  2. Allowed Origins was entered as 'akashic.no/' WITH A TRAILING SLASH, which Console stores verbatim. Measured: Origin: https://akashic.no -> 401; Origin: https://akashic.no/ -> 200. Browsers never send a path in Origin, so every real visitor would have got 401 while a curl matching the stored string passed.
